More than a billion years ago, two black holes were circling each other. Faster, and faster.
Each one, about thirty times the mass of our Sun.
Then, in a fraction of a second, they collided. Three Suns' worth of mass, gone. Turned into pure ripples in spacetime.
For that one moment, the collision out-powered every star in the observable universe. Combined.
The ripples raced outward at the speed of light, crossing the dark for more than a billion years.
Until, on September fourteenth, twenty fifteen, they finally reached a small blue world.
And this time, someone was listening. Lie-go. Two laser beams, in tunnels four kilometres long.
As the wave passed, it stretched one arm, and squeezed the other.
By one thousandth the width of a proton.
That is like measuring the distance to the nearest star, to within the width of a human hair.
The whole signal lasted just two tenths of a second.
Einstein predicted these waves in nineteen sixteen. A century later, we felt the universe tremble.
